details:
Q1: Which paths should require a trusted grant before the implement commit can include them?
Choices:
A. `.github/workflows/**` only (the path `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` guards today).
B. The full automation set the repo already treats as protected: `.github/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `workflow-templates/` (same set as the review-blocked fix's `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` rule). (RECOMMENDED)
C. Option B plus `validation/`, `ai-memory/`, `db/contracts/`, and agent-instruction files (the deterministic-skip protected list).
**Note:** in this source repo almost every orchestrator sub-issue edits `scripts/`. B and C rely on Q2 treating pipeline-authored issues as trusted, or those issues will be blocked.
Q2: What should count as the "trusted workflow record" that grants exact automation paths for an issue?
Choices:
A. A `files_touched:` allowlist in the issue body, honoured for automation paths only when the issue author is the pipeline's `GH_PAT` login (orchestrator / judge / heal-created issues) or has OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR association. Outsider-authored allowlists never grant automation paths. (RECOMMENDED)
B. A separate marker comment (e.g. `<!-- ai:automation-path-grant:v1 paths=... -->`) posted by the pipeline login or an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, listing the exact paths. The issue body is never trusted.
C. A label (e.g. `ai:allow-automation-edits`) applied by an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, verified through the label event's actor, combined with the issue's `files_touched` list for exact paths.
Q3: What should happen to the existing `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` variable (default `'true'`, documented and used by implement, review_autofix, update_workflows, orchestrate_poll)?
Choices:
A. Keep the name and its default for backward compatibility, but make it necessary-not-sufficient in `implement.yml`: automation paths also need the Q2 grant. `false` still blocks everything. Other workflows are unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Flip the `implement.yml` default to `'false'`, so automation edits need both the variable set to `true` by the operator and the Q2 grant. This is a behaviour change for consumers that rely on the current default.
Q4: When an issue has no `files_touched` block, or a malformed one, how should the scope guard behave?
Choices:
A. Fail closed only when the staged changes include a Q1 automation path. Issues that touch only ordinary source files keep today's skip behaviour. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Fail closed for every implementation commit without a valid `files_touched` block, whatever paths it touches. This blocks most standalone human-filed issues.
